title: Flight Sergeant J Hannah VC - Rose Garden
memorial_details:
description: Retford, Worksop, Isle of Axholme and Gainsborough News - Friday 06 October 1978 Page 11
The men of Squadron 83 reunite at Scampton 
A FIRST reunion of former members of one of the most distinguished war-time Royal Air Force bomber squadrons, No. 83, which flew mainly from Lincolnshire bases and was dishanded in 1969, is to be held at RAF Scampton and in Lincoln Cathedral on Saturday and Sunday, November 4 and 5. 
No 83 was the first Lancaster squadron of the Pathfinder Force. The late Sergeant John Hannah was awarded the Victoria Cross while flying with it from Scampton, where there are commemorative roses of the colour of his V.C. ribbon. 
The Squadron was equipped with Vulcans when it was dishanded at Scampton in 1969 
Founded in 1938 with Hawker Hinds, it flew successively Hampdens, Manchesters and Lancasters during the war, mainly from Scampton and Coningsby, but also for a while from Wyton (Hunts.) 
Two former squadron members, Ronald Low, of 2 St. Mark’s Road, Humberston, Grimsby, and Kenneth Cook, of 9 Prebend Lane, Welton, have worked for a long time tracking down some 200 men who served with No 83, and expect 130 to attend the re-union in the officers’ mess at Scampton (Commanding Officer Group Captain Clive Herbert) on Saturday, November 4. 
The next day they will attend mattins in Lincoln Cathedral at 11am, when those who gave their lives during the war while flying with the squadron will be specially remembered. 
After mattins there will be a dedication in the Airmen’s Chapel of the Cathedral of a commemorative plaque placed under the laid up standard of No. 83 Squadron. 
In the Airmen’s Chapel are the Memorial Books of No 1 and 5 Groups, RAF Bomber Command, containing the names of over 22,000 wartime aircrew who during the war flew missions from Lincolnshire bases and did not return. Many of them were from No. 83 Squadron. 
People from Holland who helped shot down squadron members there have been invited
